fixes.explanation: I get it, it's a river, so water feels like the obvious pick. Good river instinct, friend! But the LORD asks for something else: twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan (Joshua 4:3). Joshua tells each man to take a stone upon his shoulder (Joshua 4:5). Jars of water never come up in the passage.

Visiting traders! Friend, I love the thinking. A stranger rolls in, sees twelve big stones, and has questions. But Joshua doesn't mention a single trader. He says the ones asking will be "your children" (Joshua 4:6). The stones are a sign among the Israelites themselves.

Boundary! I see you, friend, a stone marking a line is a real thing. But Joshua doesn't say a word about lines. He calls these stones a memorial to the Israelites forever (Joshua 4:7). They're tied to the waters of the Jordan being cut off before the ark, so they point back to what happened.

The passage does not say nobody carried jars on the trip, or that stones were the only things carried.
The explanation invents a stranger visiting the camp and seeing the stones, then suggests the children’s question would probably come at the dinner table. The passage gives neither scene.
